gloss: to step closer, to compromise, to meet halfway

forms.negative: {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りませんでした

forms.label: ている polite
forms.negative: {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}っていません

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}っていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.affirmative: {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}っていました
forms.negative: {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}っていませんでした

forms.negative: {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}らなかったら

definitions.explanation: To physically walk toward someone or something.

definitions.gloss: to compromise, to make concessions, to meet halfway
definitions.explanation: To adjust one's position or opinion to reach agreement. Often implies mutual effort from both sides to bridge differences.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}がこちらに{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}ってきた。
{子|こ}どもが{母親|ははおや}のそばに{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}った。
examples.english: The child walked up to the mother.

examples.japanese: {見知|みし}らぬ{男|おとこ}がゆっくりと{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}ってきたので{緊張|きんちょう}した。
examples.english: I got nervous when a stranger slowly approached me.

examples.japanese: お{互|たが}いに{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}ることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to meet each other halfway.

examples.japanese: {双方|そうほう}が{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}らなければ{解決|かいけつ}しない。
examples.english: It won't be resolved unless both sides make concessions.

examples.japanese: {労使|ろうし}{交渉|こうしょう}で{経営側|けいえいがわ}がようやく{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}る{姿勢|しせい}を{見|み}せた。
examples.english: In the labor-management negotiations, the management side finally showed a willingness to compromise.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb ({歩|あゆ}む + {寄|よ}る). The figurative sense of compromising is the more common usage in modern Japanese. Conjugates as a godan verb: {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}らない, {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}ります, {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}って.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{互|たが}いに{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}る: to compromise with each other
- {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}る{姿勢|しせい}: willingness to compromise
- {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りを{見|み}せる: to show willingness to compromise

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {妥協|だきょう}する: to compromise (more direct, can imply reluctant concession)
- {譲歩|じょうほ}する: to make a concession (formal, one-sided yielding)
